name: Xvfb virtual display
description: Installs Xvfb and the shared libraries GUI programs need to render into it — X client libraries, software OpenGL (Mesa llvmpipe) and a base font by default; Vulkan (lavapipe) and screenshot/input tools as opt-in groups, and any extra packages an application needs — plus `xvfb-ensure`, which starts or reuses a virtual display and prints the DISPLAY to export. Sets no DISPLAY globally and starts nothing unless asked.

x11Libraries.description: Install the generic X client libraries a GUI program links or dlopens to open a window at all: libx11-6, libxext6, libxi6, libxrandr2, libxcursor1, libxinerama1, libxrender1, libxkbcommon0, libfontconfig1. For Godot (which dlopens them when not running --headless) and Aseprite. Off leaves only Xvfb itself, for a program that brings its own.

openGL.description: Install software OpenGL — libgl1, libegl1 and libgl1-mesa-dri (Mesa llvmpipe) — so a GL client renders real frames into the virtual display with no GPU. For Godot's GL Compatibility renderer (`--rendering-driver opengl3`) and Aseprite.

fonts.description: Install fonts-dejavu-core, one base font. For anything that draws text: fontconfig with no font installed renders none, which looks like a working program with blank labels.

vulkan.description: Install software Vulkan — libvulkan1 and mesa-vulkan-drivers (Mesa lavapipe). For Godot's Forward+ and Mobile renderers; the default GL Compatibility path does not need it.

tools.description: Install imagemagick and xdotool, which operate on the display itself: a screenshot of the whole X screen (`import -window root shot.png`) and synthetic keyboard/mouse input. For driving and inspecting any GUI program; Godot's own frame capture (--write-movie) does not need it.

extraPackages.description: Comma-separated apt packages to install alongside the groups, for one application's own runtime dependencies — the README carries the list VS Code / Electron extension tests need. A name ending in `t64` falls back to the same name without the suffix on a base that predates Ubuntu 24.04's rename (Ubuntu 22.04, Debian bookworm), so one list works on both.

display.description: Display number `xvfb-ensure` starts on by default — digits only, so "99" means DISPLAY=:99. If that number is taken by something that is not a working server, the next five are tried in turn. `xvfb-ensure --display <N>` overrides it per call.

screen.description: Size and colour depth of the virtual screen `xvfb-ensure` starts, as <width>x<height>x<depth> with a depth of 8, 16, 24 or 32. `xvfb-ensure --screen <WxHxD>` overrides it per call.

startOnContainerStart.description: Run `xvfb-ensure` on every container start, so a display is already up before anything asks for one. It still sets no DISPLAY: add `"remoteEnv": { "DISPLAY": ":99" }` to your own devcontainer.json if every process should use it (the README has the two lines). Off — the default — starts nothing until something calls `xvfb-ensure`.
